answer.text: Electron transport continues while ATP synthesis collapses
answer.line: The leak drains the proton gradient. The chain still pumps, but ATP synthase has nothing left to run on.

steps: Put the gradient in the middle. Electron transport pumps H+ into the lumen; ATP synthase spends that gradient to make ATP.
Make the membrane leak and H+ slips back without turning ATP synthase. The gradient is gone, so ATP synthesis collapses.
Nothing blocked the carriers. Light still drives electrons from water to NADP+, and with no gradient pushing back they may run faster.

choices.text: Both electron transport and ATP synthesis speed up together
choices.note: Electron transport can run faster with no gradient pushing back. ATP synthesis cannot rise once the gradient is gone.

choices.text: Electron transport continues while ATP synthesis collapses
choices.note: The pumps keep pumping; the turbine stops. That is uncoupling.

choices.text: Water splitting stops while NADPH production continues
choices.note: NADPH production does continue, but its electrons come from water splitting, so water splitting keeps going too.

choices.text: Electron transport halts while ATP synthesis continues
choices.note: The leak hits the gradient, not the carriers. So the chain keeps going, and ATP synthesis is what stops.

choices.text: The Calvin cycle speeds up because more protons reach the stroma
choices.note: Protons leaking into the stroma do no work. The Calvin cycle needs ATP, so it slows.

lockIt: An uncoupler drains the gradient: electron transport keeps running, ATP synthesis stops. Chloroplast or mitochondrion, same rule.
hook: Pumps keep pumping. The turbine stops.

visual.alt: A slice of thylakoid membrane, stroma above and lumen below. Electrons still run through photosystem II, cytochrome b6f and photosystem I to NADPH, and water splitting and b6f still load H+ into the lumen, but H+ leaks straight back through a hole in the membrane, outlined as the answer. ATP synthase sits idle; no ATP is made.
visual.caption: Follow the H+ arrows. With the leak open, they skip ATP synthase entirely.
